We also prove that if $C_1$ and $C_2$ are smooth curves over $k$ of positive genera $g_1$ and $g_2$ with $g_1+g_2\leq 5$, then there is a smooth curve over $k$ of genus $g_1+g_2$ whose Jacobian has the same Newton polygon as $\text{Jac}(C_1)\times\text{Jac}(C_2)$. This verifies Oort's amalgamation conjecture in total genus at most five.

papers.title: The Alon–Tarsi (1992) conjecture: for n > 2, congruences modulo divisors of (n!)³ can prove it only at Drisko's orders
papers.abstract: A Latin square of even order is even or odd according to the product of the signs of its rows and columns, read as permutations. The Alon–Tarsi conjecture (1992) says that for every even n the numbers L^e_n and L^o_n of even and odd Latin squares of order n are different. Drisko proved it for n = p + 1, p an odd prime (Drisko's orders), by showing that p^3 does not divide L^e_n − L^o_n; here p^3 divides (n!)^3, the order of the group that renames the rows, the columns and the symbols. Stones and Wanless observed that a congruence modulo a divisor of (n!)^3 can prove the conjecture at order n only through a prime factor of c_n = (n!)^3 / gcd(L^e_n − L^o_n, (n!)^3). They found c_n for n ≤ 9, and their results show that no prime q with n/2 < q < n − 1 divides it. We determine c_n for every even n ≥ 8: c_n = n − 1 if n − 1 is prime, and c_n = 1 otherwise. So, for n > 2, such congruences can prove the conjecture at Drisko's orders and only there, and the smallest open order, 26, needs a different method. The main tool is an exact identity expressing L^e_n − L^o_n, up to sign, as (n − 1)! times a circuit-partition-polynomial value for the complete directed graph with two loops at each vertex. Successive vertex removals give a quadratic lower bound for the exponent of each fixed prime. A separate signed count of fixed Latin squares handles q = n/2. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: The Avkhadiev–Wirths (2006) generalized Goodman conjecture is true
papers.abstract: Let f be meromorphic and one-to-one in the unit disk, with a simple pole at a point p in (0, 1), f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1. Its Taylor coefficients a_n at the origin satisfy the sharp bound |a_n| ≤ A_n(p) = (1 − p^{2n})/((1 − p^2)p^{n−1}). Goodman conjectured this bound, and Jenkins showed that it follows from the Bieberbach conjecture, now de Branges' theorem. Let h be a holomorphic self-map of the disk with h(0) = 0. Then f ∘ h may have poles, but it is holomorphic near 0. In 2006 Avkhadiev and Wirths conjectured that its Taylor coefficients satisfy the same bound. Their 2009 book named this the generalized Goodman conjecture. It is the meromorphic counterpart of Rogosinski's generalized Bieberbach conjecture, which de Branges' work settled. It was known for n ≤ 2, for n = 3 with p < 0.7, for n ≥ 4 with p < 1/(2n − 2), and for some classes of f. We prove it for every n and every p. The proof combines three tools: Rogosinski's reduction, by which the nth Taylor coefficient of f ∘ h equals the nth coefficient of Ef, for a holomorphic E with |E| ≤ 1 that depends on n; Jenkins' conformal map of the disk slit along [p, 1) onto the disk, a map that fixes 0 and has positive coefficients of z, z^2, z^3, …; and Robertson's inequality for odd univalent functions. For n ≥ 2, equality holds only when f(z) = z/((1 − pz)(1 − z/p)) and h is a rotation. As a consequence, we prove two conjectures of Avkhadiev and Wirths (2008): sharp bounds for the derivatives of a meromorphic map from the disk, or from a convex domain, into a simply connected domain of the sphere. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: The Avkhadiev–Wirths (2006) generalized Goodman conjecture is true, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: Let f be meromorphic and one-to-one in the unit disk, with a simple pole at a point p in (0, 1), f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1. Its Taylor coefficients a_n at the origin satisfy the sharp bound |a_n| ≤ A_n(p) = (1 − p^{2n})/((1 − p^2)p^{n−1}). Their 2009 book named this the generalized Goodman conjecture. It is the meromorphic counterpart of Rogosinski's generalized Bieberbach conjecture, which de Branges' work settled. It was known for n ≤ 2, for n = 3 with p < 0.7, for n ≥ 4 with p < 1/(2n − 2), and for some classes of f. We prove it for every n and every p. The proof combines three tools: Rogosinski's reduction, by which the nth Taylor coefficient of f ∘ h equals the nth coefficient of Ef, for a holomorphic E with |E| ≤ 1 that depends on n; Jenkins' conformal map of the disk slit along [p, 1) onto the disk, a map that fixes 0 and has positive coefficients of z, z^2, z^3, …; and Robertson's inequality for odd univalent functions. As a consequence, we prove two conjectures of Avkhadiev and Wirths (2008): sharp bounds for the derivatives of a meromorphic map from the disk, or from a convex domain, into a simply connected domain of the sphere. We also prove the following. When h has a zero of order at least d at 0 and n ≥ d, the nth coefficient is at most A_m(p) in modulus, with m = ⌊n/d⌋, and this bound is attained exactly when m divides n; for d = 2 and n = 5 we find the exact maximum. For n ≥ 2, near-extremal coefficients force f and h near their extremal forms. Finally, a sharp bound for the derivatives of a meromorphic map from any simply connected source domain Ω at a point z_0, in terms of a single number τ(Ω, z_0), gives both bounds of 2008 and also covers sources that contain ∞. The numbered results of Sections 1–5 (the focused version) are verified in Lean.

papers.title: The Complexity of Factoring Sums of Cycles
papers.abstract: A sum of directed cycles represents a finite dynamical system whose transition map is a permutation. Its decomposition into a direct product of two nontrivial systems is a classical algorithmic problem, also studied as conjugated tensor decomposition of a permutation. We establish its decision and counting complexity. For explicit transition tables, deciding nontrivial factorization is NP-complete, and counting unordered nontrivial factor pairs up to isomorphism is \#P-complete under parsimonious reductions. The reduction classifies every nontrivial factor pair: for suitable sums $A,B$ of odd-length cycles, the nontrivial pairs of $B+C_2A$ are exactly $\{A,X+C_2\}$ with $AX=B$, where $C_2$ is a two-cycle. Both factors are irreducible, and the target $B+C_2A$ has $|B|+2|A|$ states. We give a self-contained parsimonious reduction from 3-SAT to the required division instances, including the decoding of arbitrary quotients and a polynomial bound on the explicit state space. For binary cycle-list encodings, a sparse-witness argument gives NP-completeness as well. We also give an elementary proof of the output-length obstruction to \#P membership for counting all binary factor pairs, a consequence of earlier bounds on the number of quotients.

papers.title: The Esperet–Hendrey–Lagoutte–Marseloo–Norin–Steiner (2025) flow reconfiguration problem: a positive answer (k = 40)
papers.abstract: Given an oriented finite multigraph $G$ and an abelian group $\Gamma$, a nowhere-zero $\Gamma$-flow assigns each edge a value in $\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$ with equal incoming and outgoing sums at every vertex. The reconfiguration graph $F(G,\Gamma)$ connects two nowhere-zero $\Gamma$-flows when the support of their difference is a cycle; write $M_k(G)=F(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$, and let $I_k(G)$ be the analogous graph on integer flows $F$ with $1\le|F(e)|\le k-1$ on every edge. Problem 1.2 of Esperet, Hendrey, Lagoutte, Marseloo, Norin, and Steiner (2025) asked whether a uniform integer $k\ge 5$ independent of $G$ makes $I_k(G)$ connected for every finite bridgeless loopless multigraph $G$; previously only the graph-dependent bound $k=36\,|E(G)|(|V(G)|+1)$ was known. We answer Problem 1.2 positively: $I_k(G)$ is connected for every finite bridgeless loopless multigraph $G$ (and $M_k(G)$ is connected with loops allowed) whenever $k$ is a positive multiple of $40$, $48$, or $66$—in particular for $k=40$. We also prove that $F(G,\Gamma)$ is connected for every finite bridgeless multigraph $G$ and every finite abelian group $\Gamma$ that is not cyclic of prime-power order and whose order has a divisor $d$ with $4\le d\le|\Gamma|/10$. In particular, every abelian group of order $40$ works, lowering the smallest order of a group (with $|\Gamma|\ge 3$) proved universal in Esperet et al. (2025) from $|\mathbb{F}_2^8|=256$ to $40$. Both results follow from a single master theorem for reconfiguration under a restricted set of steps in a quotient $\Gamma/B$, combined with a Markov-chain averaging lemma in direct products and a lifting lemma for proper-divisor steps in $\mathbb{Z}_k$. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: The Exact Joint Spectral Envelope of the Second-Largest Adjacency and Laplacian Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: For finite simple connected graphs on at least two vertices, write $\lambda_2$ and $\mu_2$ for the second-largest adjacency and ordinary Laplacian eigenvalues. We determine $F(t)=\inf\{\mu_2(G):\lambda_2(G)\ge t\}$ for all $0\le t\le2$ and classify every minimizer. A double-star staircase accumulates at $1$. Above $\sqrt3$ there are twenty transition levels followed by an infinite sequence of six-level blocks beginning at the smallest possible index $4$. The proof combines a sharp maximum-degree reduction, explicit Schur-complement comparisons valid on algebraic intervals, and finite certificates based on exact characteristic-polynomial root counts. We also obtain the optimal coefficient $8/\sqrt3$ in a quadratic lower bound and the exact gap for nonstars in Cazenave's inequality.

papers.title: The Lorentzian Calderón problem
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness for Calderón's inverse problem on Lorentzian manifolds. More precisely, if two globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metrics agree with the Minkowski metric outside a compact set and have the same exterior measurements for waves, we prove that the metrics are equal up to a diffeomorphism that is the identity in the exterior. A similar result was proved in \cite{ORS26} if one of the metrics was close to Minkowski. More generally, we prove that the Minkowski exterior condition can be replaced by another geometric condition when recovering a metric or a potential. We also give counterexamples showing that some geometric condition is needed. The proof is based on a layer stripping approach, where the local uniqueness step is provided by a localized version of the weighted $L^2$ estimates for plane waves in \cite{ORS26}. The localization is made possible by a geometric reduction adapted from \cite{KLU18}.

papers.title: The order of excluded minors for surfaces
papers.abstract: Each closed surface $S$ has a finite list of excluded minors, and a graph embeds in $S$ if and only if none of its minors are on the list. How many vertices can these excluded minors have? Houdaigoui and Kawarabayashi conjectured an almost linear upper bound in the Euler genus $g$ of $S$. For nonorientable surfaces, we prove the conjecture by showing that every excluded minor has $O\!\left(g(\log g)^2(\log\log g)^2\right)$ vertices as $g\to\infty$. For orientable surfaces, we disprove it by exhibiting an excluded minor with $(g+2)^2$ vertices for every even $g\ge2$.

papers.title: The Rhythm of Primes: On the Formally Verified Proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: We give a complete account of a proof, due to L. Alpöge working with Claude, that no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in the half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$; in particular every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $1/2$. The proof was found and formalised in Lean 4; we follow the shorter formalisation grh-lean, which we rebuilt and checked, and each statement of the paper is tied to the Lean declarations that prove it. The argument is a descendant of Stepanov's method for curves over finite fields. A one-sided bound for a weighted sum of the von Mangoldt function over a residue class, whose weights $1-\chi_K(n)$ come from an imaginary quadratic field, excludes zeros by Landau's theorem on Dirichlet integrals of one sign. The bound is proved by comparing two estimates for chains of $m\asymp\sqrt x$ theta lifts between definite unitary groups over a CM field: an upper bound, in which the divisibility of derivatives of theta functions of CM elliptic curves at each prime reproduces the prime sums, and a lower bound from a product formula for Gram determinants, in which each prime reads the integral structure through its own twist and the norms of the lifts are Hecke $L$-values controlled by the Rallis inner product formula and by congruences, bounded through Selmer groups of anticyclotomic twists. A second-moment estimate shows that few translates of a Poincaré series span the space of target forms. The main term cancels between the two estimates, and the remainder is bounded by $x^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$.

papers.title: The Zalcman conjecture for all sufficiently large indices
papers.abstract: We prove the Zalcman conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$. More precisely, there exists an integer $N\ge3$ such that every normalized univalent function $f(z)=z+\sum_{j=2}^{\infty}a_jz^j$ in the unit disk satisfies \[ |a_n^2-a_{2n-1}|\le(n-1)^2,\qquad n\ge N, \] with equality if and only if $f$ is a rotation of the Koebe function.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Entropic Domains for TSP Complexity via 3-SAT: Foundations of the GCT-STL Research Program on P versus NP
papers.abstract: In the context of the P versus NP problem, this paper establishes the mathematical foundations of the GCT-STL research program using $TSP_{dec}$ as a canonical NP-complete representative and its polynomial reduction to 3-SAT with an exact materialized 3-CNF artifact. The framework is organized into four interacting systems: a Fundamental Mathematical Representation System, a Logical and Computational-Complexity Formal System, a Computational-Heuristic-Experimental and Simulation System, and a transversal Mathematical and Symbolic Formalization and Certification System, complemented by an AI-Assisted Neuro-Symbolic Discovery and Formalization Layer. Within the Fundamental Mathematical Representation System, nine provenance-controlled descriptors D1–D9 are organized across three computational-information domains: semantic/geometric (S), temporal/computational (T), and logical/syntactic (L). They are assembled into the canonical raw Valiant–González tensorial signature $R0:=T_{VG}^{raw}$, supported by explicit SourceMap and Provenance Bundle contracts and by three foundational entropy results. Paper I-A situates R0 within the branched four-representation architecture $R0 \rightarrow R1=L_{VG}$ and $R0 \rightarrow R2=T_{VG}^{H} \rightarrow R3=R_{VG}$, where R1 is a componentwise logarithmic scale complement, R2 the canonical entropic/information representation, and R3 the exact-envelope normalized representation. The Full STL Tensorial Coupling Principle remains an open and falsifiable hypothesis concerning a possible obstruction in the complete coupled S–T–L structure rather than in any individual domain. The logical-complexity system defines $Cost_{STL},P_{STL},NP_{STL}$, and the minimal route $F1:P\subseteq P_{STL}$; $F2:TSP_{dec}\notin P_{STL}$; $F3_{std}:TSP_{dec}\in NP$; and the conditional bridge $F4:F1\land F2\land F3_{std}\Rightarrow P\neq NP$. F1 and F2 remain open; empirical robustness and candidate obstructions remain discovery-level, while universality, representation transfer, and lower-bound transfer remain theorem-level obligations. Accordingly, Paper I-A does not prove P ≠ NP; it establishes the representational, logical, and methodological foundations for the subsequent GCT-STL program, whose companion papers develop the full four-representation mathematics, the logical-computational and heuristic-experimental architectures, formalization and certification, and the later experimental and obstruction-theoretic stages.

papers.title: Three-generated matrix algebras containing a four-regular element
papers.abstract: Let A, B, C be pairwise commuting complex n by n matrices. We prove that the dimension of the algebra they generate is at most n whenever this algebra contains an element whose eigenspaces all have dimension at most four. The eigenvalues and Jordan block lengths are arbitrary. The proof reduces to commuting nilpotent operators, studies the top and socle of a minimal counterexample, and uses a canonical-module minor identity to bound an extension with a curvilinear quotient. A change of generators then treats a four-regular element anywhere in the generated algebra. The matrix theorem is verified in Lean.

papers.title: Topology of amplituhedra
papers.abstract: We prove that the amplituhedron is homeomorphic to a closed ball for arbitrary positive external data when $m=2$, or when $m$ is positive and even and $n-k-m=3$. For $m=2$, we also prove that every source fiber is a closed ball and every open Lam stratum is an open ball. For $m=4$, we establish the convexity of complete Grassmann linear sections and show that the boundary has the homotopy type of a sphere. We further prove contractibility for $m=3,4$ and establish quantitative estimates for Plücker forms and lifting maps.

papers.title: Tracial joint spectral measures and Hanner inequalities
papers.abstract: We construct a positive tracial joint spectral measure for every bounded self-adjoint pair in a finite von Neumann algebra equipped with a faithful normal tracial state. For pencils invertible in every real direction, we obtain a density from Brown's logarithmic potential formula. A \(2\times2\) enlargement and a norm limit extend positivity to arbitrary pencils. Consequently, every real two-dimensional subspace of a Haagerup \(L_p\)-space embeds real-linearly and isometrically into a commutative \(L_p\)-space for \(0<p<\infty\). This gives the Hanner inequalities for \(1\le p<\infty\). Further consequences include commuting matrix models for shuffle traces with a fixed even number of occurrences and a sign theorem for higher-order spectral shift functions of bounded tracial Schatten perturbations in semifinite von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Two-sided bounds for site percolation on the square lattice
papers.abstract: For independent site percolation on the infinite square lattice with nearest-neighbor adjacency, we prove 0.55855 ≤ p_c ≤ 0.63345. For the lower bound we thin the children of a two-layer exploration according to their joint outcomes. A missing-neighbor constraint and bounds on the posterior of each explored column give stochastic domination at every depth. For the upper bound we couple boundary partitions on two offset tilings by 4 × 4 blocks. An intermediate occupation field with independent factors of sizes 9, 3, 3, 1 respects both tilings. Integer transports certify both couplings. Relative to the endpoints 0.556921 and 0.6463 in Niedbala Giraudin's 2026 preprint, the lower bound increases by 0.001629 and the upper bound decreases by 0.01285. The finite certificates and independent checking programs accompany the paper.

papers.title: Units in the Ring of Values of Siegel E-Functions in the Broad Sense
papers.abstract: We determine the units in the ring of values at algebraic points of Siegel $E$-functions in the broad sense. They are precisely the numbers $\alpha e^\beta$ with $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times$ and $\beta\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. Starting from an inverse relation between two values, we use division by an algebraic zero to obtain a relation in the fibre of a finite differential module. A common tensor comparison preserves this relation and, after a finite Kummer covering, can be chosen globally over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ and normalized at the evaluation point. Its analytic realization produces two reciprocal functions with algebraic Laurent coefficients and controlled growth. We then prove directly that such a function is an algebraic constant times an integral power of the variable times the exponential of a polynomial with algebraic coefficients. Evaluation at the normalized point gives the unit classification. The proof applies directly to the broad class; the corresponding statement for the strict class follows as a corollary.

papers.title: Visible prime factors under neighbouring critical divisor weights
papers.abstract: A positive divisor weight marks one prime $P$ of an integer $X<n\le2X$. We compare the law of $(n,P)$ before and after reweighting at $n+2$. For fixed $t\ge0$ and $u\to\infty$ with $u=o(\log X)$, the total variation distances for the exact cofactor $n/P$, the mark $P$ and the origin $n$ tend to $0$, $e^{-t}$ and $1$, respectively. When further factors are revealed in uniform order, the distance equals the probability, under the first law, of exhausting the factorisation up to $o(1)$, uniformly over stopping rules. A second deletion compares all incomplete records. We also determine the joint law of $n/P$, the exact neighbouring mark and the neighbouring prime divisors up to $y=X^{o(1)}$. The approximation is in total variation, with conditional error tending to zero in mean over the cofactor. At $y=X^{1/V}$ the reference conditioned on a visible neighbouring mark has distance $e^{-u/V}+o(1)$. The mark, the other small primes and the full factor count give independent exponential, Poisson-process and Gaussian limits on their respective scales.
